prompt: In a laboratory experiment to determine g using a falling ball, state two distinct advantages of using an electronic timer triggered by an electromagnet and stopped by a trapdoor, compared to using a handheld stopwatch.
hints: Consider typical human reaction time (~0.2 s) compared to fall times (~0.4 s).
Consider the precision / scale division of electronic timing.
solution:
1. Eliminates human reaction time at both release and impact.
2. Provides high resolution and precision (millisecond timing) suitable for measuring small fall times.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Human reaction time is around 0.2 s, which is a very large fraction of typical lab drop times.
Step 2: Electronic triggering eliminates this human timing error entirely.
Step 3: Electronic timers read to 0.001 s (milliseconds), offering far greater precision.

mark_scheme.criterion: Eliminates human reaction time (or avoids reaction time error)
Provides higher resolution / precision (e.g. milliseconds) / reduces percentage uncertainty
